title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This page tries to discover the relationship between film runtime and IMDb ratings. Figure 1 shows this relationship in a scatter plot.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.title("Runtime vs. IMDb Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtime vs. IMDb rating

title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page explores the relationship between film production budgets and worldwide revenues. Figure 1 shows the relationship using a scatter plot.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue")
plt.title("Budget vs. Revenue")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film production budget vs. worldwide revenue

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

The Bond films in this dataset were released between 1995 and 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Release Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (million USD)")
plt.title("James Bond Box Office Revenue")
plt.show()







Figure 1: James Bond worldwide revenue over time

title: Box Office Numbers
text: This website explores a dataset of 104 films released between 1980 and 2025. The dataset includes film budgets, worldwide revenues, runtimes, IMDb ratings, and franchise information. The figures are approximation and are not adjusted for inflation.
